main_statement.latex: For every integer n>=2 there is a constant L_n>=1 with the following property. Let K in R, and let (X,d,H^n_d) be a noncollapsed RCD(K,n) space. Let p in X. If every pointed Gromov--Hausdorff tangent of X at p is pointed-isometric to (R^n,|.|,0), then there exist an open neighborhood U of p, an open set V subset R^n, and a homeomorphism F:U->V such that L_n^{-1}d(x,z) <= |F(x)-F(z)| <= L_n d(x,z) (x,z in U). The distance on the left and right is the original distance d restricted to U.
main_statement.paraphrase: In a noncollapsed RCD(K,n) space (measure = n-dim Hausdorff measure), every point whose tangents are all Euclidean has an open neighbourhood that is bi-Lipschitz (for the ambient metric) to an open subset of R^n, with distortion depending only on n; the neighbourhood size depends on X and p.

headline_corollaries.paraphrase: An open set of full H^n-measure containing all regular points carries a countable L_n-bi-Lipschitz atlas with L_n^2-bi-Lipschitz transitions. Uses DPG18 Thm 1.12 (regular set has full measure).

main_statement.catalog_mismatch: CONTENTS.md:8665 and overview.tex:812 say the chart has 'a point-dependent finite constant'; the paper (abstract paper.tex:47-48, Thm introduction.tex:18-19, proof renormalization.tex:836-838) claims L_n depends only on n. The catalogue summary is weaker (possibly from an earlier version); the paper's stronger claim is what is analysed.
main_statement.note_for_comparator: No Lean comparator. The theorem is the full regular-point conjecture as recalled in HZ26 Sec 1.2 (which attributes it to CC97) under the stated noncollapsed RCD hypotheses.

Analyst observation (NOT claimed by the paper): since the singular set of a noncollapsed space has codimension >= 2, Cor 1.2 would also answer, in local-chart form, Naber's Open Problem 2.2 (arXiv 2010.10031: 'bi-Lipschitz to a manifold away from a set of codimension two?') for noncollapsed Ricci limits, and would give a (non-harmonic) bi-Lipschitz chart at the special point of the Colding-Naber example (Naber's Example 2.3), where harmonic and distance coordinates provably fail.

cited_or_new.cue: 'The two-center directional bound displayed above is proved here in the form needed for the value-space construction' (introduction.tex:180-181); antecedents CC96, CJN21 named

load_bearing_guess.reason: Makes the covector field v_i small (|v_i|_Q <= sqrt(eps) r sqrt(E)) and its cutoff errors summable; without it the per-scale error is eps_i, not summable.

items.analytic_check: Not a subterm of goal or L; nearest L statement: CJN21 Thm 6.1 (L^2 Hessian of splitting maps bounded linearly by volume/entropy pinching at k+1 spanning points).

provisional_N.justification: Close variant (one-direction, two-point, value-space form) of CJN21 sharp splitting estimates; paper itself names antecedents. Could be argued N3 for the 'evaluate mass on coordinate differences' reading.

provisional_F.justification: If N3: a strengthened (directional) estimate replacing the isotropic eps H bound.

cited_or_new.cue: 'We compensate for this degeneration in the \emph{space of coordinate values}' (introduction.tex:129-130)

load_bearing_guess.reason: Representation in which the whole renormalization is done.

items.name: Patches: maximal r_i-separated nets Y_i, value-space cutoffs phi_{i,y}(P)=psi(r_i^{-1}R_i(y)^{-1/2}(P-P_y)), active sets A_i(x), sums Z_i(x), S_i(x)
items.statement: Bounded overlap |A_i(x)|<=N; net point within r_i has phi=1 (weight-one centre).

items.name: Fixed patch centres z_{i,y} nearly minimizing E_i on the patch, c_{i,y}=P_{z_{i,y}}
items.statement: E_i(z_{i,y}) < 2 inf_{x in T_{i,y}} E_i(x); positive floor guarantees existence; no measurable selection needed.

load_bearing_guess.reason: Ensures the directional bound at every active point uses E_i(x) (not a sup over the patch).

provisional_N.justification: New small selection trick, part of the field construction (graded with I41).

items.name: Covector field v_i(P)=sum_y phi_{i,y}(P) D_{i,y}(P - c_{i,y})
items.statement: Smooth field whose derivative at P_x is S_i(x)+e(xi) and whose value is O(sqrt(eps) r sqrt(E)) in Q-norm.

cited_or_new.cue: 'From the forms D_{i,y} and smooth cutoffs we build covector fields v_i' (introduction.tex:194-195)

provisional_N.justification: Localized gradient of the quadratic potentials 1/2 D[P-c]; new as a device but simple once D_{i,y} and the directional estimate are given.

provisional_F.justification: Auxiliary construction built only to drive the iteration.

items.name: Field estimates (re:field-estimates)
items.statement: r^{-1}|v_i|_Q<=C sqrt(eps E); Dv_i xi = S xi + e(xi); |S xi|_Q<=sqrt(eps Z[xi]); |e|_Q<=C sqrt(eps E)|xi|_H; |xi^T e(xi)|<=C sqrt(Z[xi]E)|xi|_H; r|D^2 v(xi,xi)|_Q <= C(sqrt(Z[xi])|xi|_H + sqrt(E)|xi|_H^2); Gevrey jets eps C_v^{m+1}(m!)^s.

load_bearing_guess.reason: All error terms of the bootstrap.

provisional_N.justification: Direct consequences of I34 + positivity; the diagonal bound (Cauchy-Schwarz before summing) is the key subtlety.

items.name: Value-space renormalization iteration h_0=Id, h_{i+1}=h_i + (Dh_i)^{-T} v_i, with the exact metric-step identity |(J+DW)xi|^2-|J xi|^2 = 2 xi^T Dv xi - 2<D^2h(xi,xi), J^{-T}v> + |DW xi|^2
items.statement: The inverse transpose turns the leading derivative of v into a positive metric increment 2S_i; the only first-order error is the diagonal second-derivative term.

cited_or_new.cue: 'The inverse transpose is chosen to turn the leading derivative of v_i directly into a change of metric' (renormalization.tex:318-319); no precedent named

load_bearing_guess.reason: Defines the chart F=lim h_i o u; the core of Section 4.

items.analytic_check: No subterm of the goal (which asks only for some chart) or of L.

provisional_N.justification: No neighbour found for a map built in coordinate-value space whose pullback metric accumulates per-scale Bochner mass forms; resembles Nash's positive-metric-increment iteration and Newton/gradient updates, but in a different setting and purpose.

provisional_F.justification: Change of representation: degeneration of the harmonic coordinates is compensated by a map on their value space (F3 secondary: auxiliary maps h_i).

items.name: Simultaneous metric + all-order Gevrey jet bootstrap: A^{-1}H_i <= J_i^TJ_i <= A H_i and r_i^{m-1}||D^m h_i||_{H_i->R^n} <= B^{m-1}(m!)^{1+sigma}
items.statement: IH carries all-order jet bounds to beat loss of one derivative per step.

cited_or_new.cue: 'We shall prove simultaneously a metric bound and all higher-derivative bounds' (renormalization.tex:339-340)

items.analytic_check: Templated IH strengthening (carry extra tracked quantity: jets; quantitative all-order version).

provisional_N.justification: Templated strengthening (capped at N2): Gevrey/analytic majorant bootstrap is standard for derivative loss.

items.name: Factorial convolution and inverse coefficients (re:inverse-majorant)
items.statement: With L_m=(m+1)((m+1)!)^sigma, sum L_l L_{m-l} <= C L_m and the inverse of J inherits jet bounds with the same base B.
items.analytic_check: Gevrey classes closed under inversion: classical.

items.name: One step for all jets (re:jet-step)
items.statement: Jet bounds propagate from level i to i+1 for eps small depending on A,sigma,B.

items.name: Uniform metric and jet bounds with the diagonal second-derivative recurrence (re:metric-iteration)
items.statement: b_i=r_i|D^2h_i(xi,xi)|/q_i obeys b_{i+1}<=b_i/2 + C_A f_i, f_i=sqrt(Z_i[xi])+sqrt(E_i)q_i; hence sum b_i^2 <= C_A H_k[xi] and ||J_k xi|^2 - |xi|^2 - 2 sum_{i<k} S_i[xi]| <= C_A(sqrt eps + eps) H_k[xi]; 'Only the sum of E_i has been used, never the sum of its square roots.'

cited_or_new.cue: 'A recurrence for these diagonal derivatives allows the errors to be summed using sum E_i, even when sum sqrt(E_i) diverges' (introduction.tex:204-206)

load_bearing_guess.reason: The metric bootstrap; produces bi-Lipschitz control of every h_i.

items.analytic_check: Not in goal or L; Euclidean analogue: square-summable conditions (Toro 1995, DT12) but via a different mechanism.

provisional_N.justification: The l^2 diagonal recurrence that pairs b_i with sqrt(E_i) q_i by Cauchy-Schwarz, so that only sum E_i is needed, is the decisive new estimate; no equivalent found.

provisional_F.justification: Together with I43: value-space representation plus the l^2 recurrence (F2 flavour: tracked quantity b_i).

items.name: The limiting chart (re:limit-chart)
items.statement: F=lim h_i o u is uniformly convergent with tail tau r_i; for x,z in B_rho(p), choose D t <= r_i < 2Dt, Taylor along segment in the central ellipsoid, metric bound and tails give (4 sqrt A)^{-1} d <= |F(x)-F(z)| <= 4 sqrt A d; invariance of domain gives open image.

items.name: Proof of Thm main: constants depend only on n; L_n = 4 sqrt(A(n))
items.statement: Fix enlargements with n, s=sigma=2; choose a late rescaling; rescale chart back.

proof_architecture.claim: Rescale at p: uniform delta-flatness of all balls at all scales <= 64T near p (Bishop-Gromov + density<=1 + DPG18), harmonic coordinates u with |grad u|<=C_n.

Harmonic normalization at every centre and dyadic scale; mean Gram R_i slowly varying (2^{2a|i-j|}); small normalized Bochner mass; u is an open homeomorphism with ellipsoid containment and scale separation.

Heat Gram Q_i monotone, H_i=Q_i^{-1} increasing (possibly unbounded); heat decrement ~ dyadic Bochner mass; non-commutative cumulative comparison Id+sum Z_i ~ H_k ~ Id+sum S_i for the local mass forms D_{i,y}.
Poisson replacements of d^2/2 with defects P_i summable by exact volume-ratio telescoping; radial invariance with sqrt(E_i) error, E_i a smoothed summable defect.
Two-centre commutator + radial transport + sharp projection: the Bochner mass of u in the direction u(x)-u(z) is <= C r_i^2 (E_i(x)+E_i(z)) (directional pinching).
On the value domain Omega build patch fields v_i=sum phi D_{i,y}(P-c_{i,y}) with near-minimizing centres; field estimates (value O(sqrt(eps E) r), derivative S_i+e, diagonal error sqrt(Z E)).
Iterate h_{i+1}=h_i+(Dh_i)^{-T}v_i. Gevrey jet bootstrap absorbs derivative loss; l^2 diagonal recurrence b_{i+1}<=b_i/2+C f_i gives |J_k xi|^2 = |xi|^2+2 sum S_i[xi] + O(sqrt eps H_k[xi]) ~ H_k[xi].

F=lim h_i o u converges with tail tau r_i; for a pair at distance t choose r_i ~ D t, Taylor in the central ellipsoid + separation => bi-Lipschitz with L_n=4 sqrt(A(n)); invariance of domain => open image.

eureka_candidates_ranked.name: Value-space renormalization: h_{i+1}=h_i+(Dh_i)^{-T}v_i with the l^2 diagonal second-derivative recurrence
eureka_candidates_ranked.for: Turns a non-summable first-order drift of the harmonic coordinates (H_k may be unbounded) into a realizable metric on a single map. The inverse transpose makes the leading change a positive sum of mass forms; the only first-order error is <D^2h(xi,xi), J^{-T}v>, handled by an l^2 recurrence that pairs with sqrt(E_i) q_i so that only sum E_i is needed. Nothing like it is in the goal or in L; it is exactly where the classical bi-Holder barrier (sum sqrt E_i = infinity) is crossed.
eureka_candidates_ranked.against: Square-summability-suffices is Toro 1995 / David-Toro (cited DT12). Iteratively adding positive metric increments with derivative-loss control is Nash's C^1 / Nash-Moser architecture. The J^{-T} update is the gradient of a potential in the pulled-back metric (natural Newton-type step). Gevrey majorants are classical. Once I22 and I34 are given, the construction may be 1-2 steps away.
eureka_candidates_ranked.quick_literature_check: WebSearch: Toro 1995 square-summable beta numbers (Duke 77); GV25 (arXiv 2406.13771) bi-Lipschitz Reifenberg under summable GH errors; Nash/Nash-Kuiper stage-step iteration with primitive metrics. No construction of a value-space map accumulating Bochner mass forms found.

correctness_audit.verdict: No gap found in the steps traced (all of Sections 3.3-3.4 and 5, the structure of Sections 3.1-3.2 and 4.2-4.4). The claim is extraordinary: it resolves a question going back to Cheeger-Colding (CC97 Rem 5.15) recalled as a conjecture in HZ26, and (unclaimed) implies Naber's Open Problem 2.2 in local-chart form. It is unrefereed and has no Lean; expert review is required.
checked: Uniform flatness at all small scales near p: Bishop-Gromov monotonicity traps volume ratios between ratio at a fixed radius (>=1-delta) and density (<=1 everywhere for noncollapsed RCD). Correct.
Telescoping of Poisson defects: mu(B_t)=(a_i-n)V(t)-t^{n+1}A'(t) and 16S r_{i+1}=8S r_i make sum_i [A(8Sr_i)-A(16Sr_i)] telescope to <= omega_n - A(16S) = o(1). Correct.
Radial transport cutoff: with A_0=2(n+4)/(R-1), -t phi' - (a+2)phi >= |phi'|+phi on (R,3R) in both sub-intervals. Checked.
Sharp projection limit: X.grad w = w + l.X + k forces degree>=2 terms to vanish, l=0, w affine; orthogonality gives contradiction. Correct.
Inverse-increment identity B_i = Q^{-1/2}((Id-E)^{-1}-Id)Q^{-1/2} and spectral bounds. Correct.
Metric-step identity: <J xi, J^{-T} Dv xi> = xi^T Dv xi and <J xi, (D_xi J^{-T}) v> = -<D^2h(xi,xi), J^{-T}v>. Correct.

Diagonal recurrence: b_{i+1} <= b_i/2 + (r_i/2q_i)|D^2W_i(xi,xi)| using q_{i+1}>=q_i; three terms bounded by C_A f_i with f_i=sqrt(Z[xi])+sqrt(E)q_i. Dimensionally consistent (degree 1 in xi). Checked.
Error sums: sum b_i q_i sqrt(E_i) <= (sum b_i^2)^{1/2}(q_k^2 sum E_i)^{1/2} <= C sqrt(eps) H_k[xi]. Correct.
Jet step: ratio of new contribution to allowance is eps C_A B 2^{1-m}(m+1)^{1+sigma}, bounded in m. Correct.
Factorial convolution delta_m -> 0 for sigma>=1 (endpoint terms O(m^{-sigma}), middle O(m^{2-3 sigma})). Correct.
Final chart: segment stays in central ellipsoid (|Delta|_H <= 2t < a r_i since D>4/a); Taylor remainder <= 4K_T t/D; tails <= 4D tau t. Correct.
consistency_checks_passed: Not over-reaching to harmonic charts: HZ26 (citing Honda-Sire, Otsu-Shioya) and Colding-Naber Example 2.3 show harmonic/distance charts can fail to be bi-Lipschitz; the paper's chart F is non-harmonic and the Gram matrix of u may degenerate (H_k unbounded is explicitly allowed).
Not over-reaching to Holder metric tensors: CN13 Thm 1.2 examples are respected (no regularity of the metric tensor claimed).
Not over-reaching to collapsed spaces (HNW25 four-dimensional limits with no manifold points): noncollapsed hypothesis is used essentially through density<=1 and volume telescoping.
Mechanism matches the known Euclidean picture: summable volume pinching ~ square-summable GH flatness, the Toro-type regime.
residual_concerns: RCD technicalities are delegated to citations with sketch justifications (capacity representatives when pairing with possibly singular Bochner measures; measure-valued Laplacians of squared distance at the centre; local test-function class for constant-Laplacian solutions).

Many uniform constants come from compactness/contradiction over infinitely many scales and centres (harmonic normalization, affine improvement, sharp projection); each is standard but the uniformity bookkeeping is delicate.

The claim that L_n depends only on n requires every compactness argument to output thresholds, not constants; the text asserts this (renormalization.tex:824-838) but it was not re-derived line by line. The catalogue summary instead says 'point-dependent finite constant'.

Lemma co:heat-comparison and co:inverse-increments involve several interlocking exponents (a<1/8, 4a<gamma, gamma=1/2 vs gamma=1/8 in pinching.tex, beta=1/16); the reuse of gamma for two different constants in different sections is harmless but error-prone.
No independent check (Lean, referee, trace). Extraordinary-claim prior should keep the correctness probability well below 1 until expert review.

extraction_friction: Almost all load-bearing objects are display-math definitions with no environment and no \emph: R_i, Q_i, H_i, N_j, F_i, D_{i,y}, Z_i, S_i, P_i, E_i, Ptilde_i, v_i, h_i, b_i, f_i. Only three \emph's (n-regular, space of coordinate values, squared), one of which is a definition.

Heavy symbol overloading: E (defect E_i, E_cut, error e(xi), annulus integral), D (D_{i,y}, Frechet D^m, constant D, distance D), A (enlargement, A_i^a(T), bootstrap A, A_a(t) volume ratio), a (centre, growth exponent, a_i Laplacian constant, vectors a_i, ellipsoid constant), gamma (1/2 in Sec 3, 1/8 in Sec 4), s (Gevrey exponent and defect s^2), L (enlargement, L_m, L_n, L_v operator).
Label prefixes (co:, pi:, re:) follow files, not section numbers; Section 3 (co:heat-section) lives in coordinates.tex.

Key sub-claims sit inside proofs: the exact metric-step identity (renormalization.tex:321-330), the diagonal recurrence (re:diagonal-recurrence), the telescoping (pinching.tex:259-275), the inline 'tau-normalizable' definition (coordinates.tex:270-280).
No Lean and no trace: load-bearing shares are from a hand-built paper DAG only.
Catalogue summary disagrees with the paper on constant dependence.
